editorial:
Imagine you are on the fast track to becoming the President of the United States. You have the brains, the looks, and all the young voters in your corner. That is exactly where Gary Hart finds himself in 1987. He is the star of the Democratic party and seems like a sure bet for the White House. The vibe is very tense and professional, showing you how high the stakes are when you are in the spotlight. You get to see how a man who thinks he is untouchable suddenly finds himself fighting for his life when a secret affair leaks to the press.

What really hits home is the acting, as you see Hart go from confident to completely broken. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow if you are not into politics. It is a great look at how the media can tear someone down in an instant. If you want to see it, renting it on Apple TV is a quick way to go, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is the best bet for the best picture. It is a solid pick for anyone who likes true stories about power and failure.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Gary Hart realizing that the media will not stop attacking him no matter what he says. He eventually drops out of the race because the scandal is too much to handle. You see him reflect on his lost dreams and how his pride played a part in his downfall. It wraps up by showing that once you lose the public's trust, it is almost impossible to get it back.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about politics and scandals.
